extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys and other practitioners before the USPTO, OED staff, and counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order resolving a USPTO disciplinary matter under the OED rules: it states jurisdictional bases, stipulated facts of misconduct, legal conclusions (specific regulatory violations), and the sanctions/conditions (suspension, monitoring, reinstatement process, publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the statutory/regulatory authority under which the Final Order and settlement are entered; required legal basis for any OED action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to resolve disciplinary action by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement submitted to the Under Secretary/Director must conform to § 11.26 procedural requirements for approval and finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the stipulation include knowingly providing false status information in client spreadsheets (claiming foreign or U.S. applications were pending when they were abandoned or never filed), fabricating serial numbers, and submitting false timesheet entries or billing for work not performed (33 entries on 17 invoices totaling $60,825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of matters entrusted
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting matters entrusted to the practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include failing to respond to foreign office actions resulting in abandonment, failing to file provisional or non-provisional applications despite work being substantially complete, and missing filing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner is suspended for a specified period (here, twenty-four (24) months) from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets the suspension term and related conditions (e.g., when reinstatement may be sought). Suspension commencement is the date the Final Order is signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspended practitioner must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the duration of the suspension (notification and practice-limitation obligations described in that rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly requires compliance and grants limited recognition (30 days) solely to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b). Noncompliance can trigger further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrowly-timed recognition is only for administrative compliance purposes and does not negate the suspension term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will promptly dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; the practitioner may not use or obtain any customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate administrative steps to prevent practice activity through USPTO systems during suspension or after noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reinstatement must show (1) good moral character and reputation, competency and learning in law as required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission; (2) resumption of practice will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; and (3) full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive criteria the OED Director will evaluate when considering a reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for filing a reinstatement petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may not file a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 during the first ninety (90) days after the Final Order is signed, but may file at any time after 90 days requesting reinstatement effective prior to expiration of the suspension, subject to the OED Director's approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order permits an early-reinstatement petition after 90 days; the OED Director can stay or grant reinstatement and may later lift a stay if noncompliance is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health-care monitoring requirement as condition of suspension/reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: For the twenty-four (24) month suspension period the practitioner must, at his own expense: (a) remain under the care of a health care professional for the clinically diagnosed condition that affected his ability to handle workload, and (b) obtain regular written reports from that professional indicating adherence to the prescribed regimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The health-care provider's reports must be submitted to the OED Director every six months, with the first due six months from the date the Final Order is signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's Order to Show Cause process for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during the suspension, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the practitioner's last address of record, and grant fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period, if the Director remains of the opinion of noncompliance, the Director will deliver the Order to Show Cause, the practitioner's response (if any), and supporting evidence to the USPTO Director and request amendment of the Final Order (e.g., extend the wait to request reinstatement) or lifting of any stay resulting in immediate suspension. The Order describes procedural steps and possible outcomes (extended ineligibility to petition up to 24 months, lifting stays, immediate suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedures if practitioner is suspended for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner is suspended pursuant to the noncompliance provisions, then (1) they must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) USPTO will dissociate the practitioner's name from customer numbers and PKI; and (4) practitioner shall not use or obtain any customer number or PKI until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies administrative consequences and public dissemination steps upon noncompliance-based suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline’s Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; the Director shall give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states of admission, to courts where the practitioner is admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting and official Gazette notice are required; the published Notice of Suspension summarizes the violations, sanction, and key facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings as (1) an aggravating factor in determining discipline for similar misconduct and/or (2) to rebut any statement or representation by or on the practitioner's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order will be part of the practitioner's disciplinary history and will influence future sanction determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating considerations: restitution, remorse, medical nexus, and favorable statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence showing restitution to clients, practitioner remorse/contrition, a nexus between misconduct and a clinically diagnosed medical condition, reduced income, and favorable statements from current/prior employers may be relied upon as mitigating facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stipulation notes that the former firm made full restitution, the respondent expressed remorse, provided evidence of a medical condition that affected workload, and principals of the current firm provided favorable statements; such factors are relevant to the negotiated sanction and future reinstatement considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED/USPTO procedural reservations and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement prevents the Office from seeking discipline under other provisions (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57) for misconduct underlying any Order to Show Cause; the OED Director and Respondent each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement preserves the Office's ability to pursue further discipline for the same misconduct and allocates no further cost liabilities between the parties.
